iterations.theme: Zašto je Vatikan pozvao AI laboratorije: događaj, enciklika Magnifica Humanitas i pitanje je li umjetna inteligencija neutralan alat

sections.subtitle: Kad Frontier laboratorij zamoli Crkvu za pomoć: pozadina vatikanskog susreta
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael Baggot objašnjava zašto je predstavnik Anthropica bio prisutan na vatikanskom događaju
sections.content:
Razgovor otvara voditelj **Matthew Harvey Sanders**, koji pozdravlja dvojicu gostiju – **oca Michaela Baggota** i **oca Kennyja Anga** – i predlaže da se prije ulaska u sam tekst enciklike *Magnifica Humanitas* najprije razmotri kontekst samog vatikanskog događaja. Sanders napominje da je i sam imao priliku biti prisutan, a da je otac Michael nekoliko tjedana kasnije proveo dodatno vrijeme u razgovorima s ljudima iz Anthropica.

Otac Michael odmah otvara ono što je najviše zasmetalo dijelu javnosti: prisutnost Chrisa, istraživača iz **Anthropica**, na vatikanskom skupu. Priznaje da su mu mnogi pisali zabrinuti zbog te prisutnosti, ali ističe da je iz izravnog kontakta bilo jasno kako se ne radi o slučajnom gostu:

- Chris se, kaže, **dugo i ozbiljno bavio razgovorima s Katoličkom Crkvom**;
- mjesecima je okupljao katoličke učenjake kako bi raspravljali o **Claudeovu "ustavu"** i ključnim načelima kojima se usmjeravaju modeli;
- njegov tim aktivno je tražio dijalog s različitim mudrosnim tradicijama, a posebno s Katoličkom Crkvom.

Otac Michael dodaje da ga je vidio i kao predstavnika šire znanstvene zajednice koja se bavi **interpretabilnošću** – pokušajem da se ti sustavi učine transparentnijima i da se razumije zašto uopće nastaju određeni rezultati. Njegova poruka na događaju, prepričava otac Michael, bila je iznenađujuće snažna i ponizna: oni koji dizajniraju te tehnologije u graničnim laboratorijima **sami nisu opremljeni** da razriješe duboka filozofska i teološka pitanja koja pritom nastaju. Potrebna im je institucija koja nije vođena ekonomskim motivima ni motivima moći, a koja može razgovor utemeljiti na antropologiji i ključnim moralnim načelima.

"Dakle, to je zapravo molba nekoga iz Frontier laboratorija da kaže: Crkvo, pomozite nam", zaključuje otac Michael, na što Sanders dodaje: "Dajte nam malo mudrosti."
sections.subtitle_en: When a Frontier laboratory asks the Church for help: the background of the Vatican meeting
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael Baggot explains why an Anthropic representative was present at the Vatican event
sections.content_en:
The conversation is opened by host **Matthew Harvey Sanders**, who welcomes two guests – **Father Michael Baggot** and **Father Kenny Ang** – and suggests that before entering into the text of the encyclical *Magnifica Humanitas* itself, the context of the Vatican event itself should first be considered. Sanders notes that he himself had the opportunity to be present, and that Father Michael spent additional time a few weeks later in conversations with people from Anthropic.

Father Michael immediately addresses what bothered a part of the public the most: the presence of Chris, a researcher from **Anthropic**, at the Vatican gathering. He admits that many wrote to him concerned about that presence, but emphasizes that from direct contact it was clear that this was not an accidental guest:

- Chris, he says, **had long and seriously engaged in conversations with the Catholic Church**;
- for months he had been gathering Catholic scholars to discuss **Claude's "constitution"** and the key principles guiding the models;
- his team actively sought dialogue with different wisdom traditions, and especially with the Catholic Church.

Father Michael adds that he also saw him as a representative of the broader scientific community dealing with **interpretability** – the attempt to make these systems more transparent and to understand why certain results arise in the first place. His message at the event, Father Michael recounts, was surprisingly powerful and humble: those who design these technologies in frontier labs **are not themselves equipped** to resolve the deep philosophical and theological questions that arise in the process. They need an institution that is not driven by economic motives or motives of power, and that can ground the conversation in anthropology and key moral principles.

"So, it is actually a plea from someone from a Frontier lab saying: Church, help us," concludes Father Michael, to which Sanders adds: "Give us a little wisdom."
keywords_en: dialogue between the Church and technology

sections.subtitle: Duga povijest kontakata i strah od 'moralnog pranja'
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Matthew Harvey Sanders postavlja pitanje o zabrinutostima zbog prisutnosti Anthropica
sections.content:
Sandersa iznenađuje podatak da je pripremni rad trajao mjesecima. Podsjeća da je i ranije postojala duga povijest otvorenog dijaloga Svete Stolice s laboratorijima – **Demis Hassabis** bio je dio Papinske akademije znanosti, a samo nekoliko tjedana prije spomenutog susreta u Rimu je održan događaj na kojem je sudjelovao i **OpenAI**.

Otac Michael pojašnjava kronologiju: s Chrisom se upoznao preko zajedničkog prijatelja jer je ovaj bio pozvan na vatikanski događaj o **dostojanstvu djeteta**. Nakon toga uslijedio je poziv katoličkim učenjacima u Washingtonu da rasprave nacrt "ustava" modela, a kasnije je Anthropic više puta pozivao katoličke učenjake, ali i predstavnike drugih vjerskih tradicija, u svoje sjedište u Kaliforniji.

Sanders potom postavlja izravno pitanje: koje su bile temeljne zabrinutosti onih koji su mu se javljali? Otac Michael ih sažima bez uljepšavanja – postojao je strah da je riječ o **triku ili taktici**: da tvrtka želi dobiti odobrenje Crkve, lijepu fotografiju, a zatim nastaviti s uobičajenim poslom ne provodeći ništa od onoga što Crkva govori.

"To bi se moglo smatrati nekom vrstom **moralnog pranja**", kaže. Priznaje da je takav stav cinična, ali razumljiva reakcija te da je opasnost od manipulacije Crkvom stvarna, zbog čega članovi Crkve trebaju ostati na oprezu. No, dodaje, iz vlastitog iskustva može potvrditi da katolički učenjaci **ne sjede pasivno** i ne prihvaćaju sve što Anthropic ima za reći.
sections.subtitle_en: A long history of contacts and fear of 'moral washing'
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Matthew Harvey Sanders asks a question about concerns regarding the presence of Anthropic
sections.content_en:
Sanders is surprised by the fact that the preparatory work lasted for months. He recalls that there had already been a long history of open dialogue of the Holy See with laboratories – **Demis Hassabis** was part of the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, and only a few weeks before the aforementioned meeting, an event took place in Rome in which **OpenAI** also participated.

Father Michael clarifies the chronology: he met Chris through a mutual friend because the latter had been invited to a Vatican event on the **dignity of the child**. After that, an invitation followed to Catholic scholars in Washington to discuss the draft "constitution" of the model, and later Anthropic repeatedly invited Catholic scholars, but also representatives of other religious traditions, to its headquarters in California.

Sanders then asks a direct question: what were the fundamental concerns of those who reached out to him? Father Michael summarizes them without sugarcoating – there was a fear that it was a **gimmick or tactic**: that the company wants to obtain the approval of the Church, a nice photo, and then continue with business as usual without implementing anything of what the Church says.

"That could be considered some kind of **moral washing**," he says. He admits that such an attitude is a cynical, but understandable reaction, and that the danger of manipulation of the Church is real, which is why members of the Church need to remain alert. But, he adds, from his own experience he can confirm that Catholic scholars **do not sit passively** and do not accept everything Anthropic has to say.

sections.subtitle: Dobrobit modela, moralni pacijenti i zašto pravila nisu dovoljna
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael Baggot objašnjava raspravu o 'model welfare' i etici vrline
sections.content:
Prema ocu Michaelu, između katoličkih učenjaka i laboratorija postoje zajednički temelji, ali i **stvarne točke napetosti** – posebno oko rasprave o **dobrobiti modela**.

Anthropic je, kaže, ozbiljno razmatrao mogu li Claude ili njihovi modeli biti **moralni pacijenti** koji zaslužuju određenu brigu i razmatranje, usporedivo s načinom na koji se odnosimo prema neljudskim životinjama. Uz to idu i pitanja o potencijalnoj svijesti sustava umjetne inteligencije. Katolički učenjaci, naglašava, tim se pitanjima **stvarno protive** i tu se vodi prava rasprava.

Druga razina rasprave je metaetička. Jedno je reći da se želi da Claude bude koristan, da ne šteti korisnicima, da bude iskren i siguran – ali odmah slijede pitanja:

- Što podrazumijevamo pod **štetom**?
- Što podrazumijevamo pod **sigurnošću**?
- Što znači etička iskrenost i **koju etiku** uopće usvajamo?

Otac Michael primjećuje da članovi Anthropica pokazuju stvaran interes za crkvenu tradiciju **etike vrline**, jer su shvatili da sama moralna pravila nisu dovoljna – da ni deontologija sama po sebi, ni čisti utilitarizam ne mogu odgovoriti na sve. No upozorava: etika vrline može se iskoristiti na vrlo različite načine, pa se odmah postavlja pitanje **koja je temeljna vizija osobe** u pozadini tih ideja o vrlini. Zaključuje da je pred svima još mnogo dijaloga, ali da je razgovor barem započeo i da se nastavlja.
sections.subtitle_en: Model welfare, moral patients and why rules are not enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael Baggot explains the debate on 'model welfare' and virtue ethics
sections.content_en:
According to Father Michael, between Catholic scholars and the labs there are common grounds, but also **real points of tension** – especially around the discussion of **model welfare**.

Anthropic, he says, seriously considered whether Claude or their models could be **moral patients** who deserve a certain care and consideration, comparable to the way we relate to non-human animals. Along with that go questions about the potential consciousness of artificial intelligence systems. Catholic scholars, he emphasizes, **really oppose** these questions, and that is where a real debate is being held.

The second level of the debate is metaethical. It is one thing to say that one wants Claude to be helpful, not to harm users, to be honest and safe – but questions immediately follow:

- What do we mean by **harm**?
- What do we mean by **safety**?
- What does ethical honesty mean and **which ethics** are we adopting at all?

Father Michael notes that members of Anthropic show a real interest in the Church's tradition of **virtue ethics**, because they have realized that moral rules alone are not enough – that neither deontology by itself, nor pure utilitarianism can answer everything. But he warns: virtue ethics can be used in very different ways, so the question immediately arises **what is the fundamental vision of the person** behind those ideas of virtue. He concludes that there is still much dialogue ahead for everyone, but that the conversation has at least begun and that it continues.

sections.subtitle: Papa je govorio engleski: poruka upućena Silicijskoj dolini
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Kenny Ang komentira detalj da je papa na događaju govorio engleski
sections.content:
Voditelj se potom obraća **ocu Kennyju Angu** i pita ga kakve je povratne informacije dobio nakon što je objavljeno da je Anthropic pozvan.

Otac Kenny ističe jedan naizgled sitan, ali vrlo govorljiv detalj: **papa je na tom događaju govorio engleski**. Podsjeća da papa obično govori talijanski, pa činjenicu da je odabrao engleski tumači kao jasan signal da se poruka upućuje **tehnološkoj zajednici u cjelini** – ljudima iz Silicijske doline i industrije. U tom smislu, kaže, i sama prisutnost predstavnika laboratorija dobiva svoj okvir: pokušaj je to započinjanja razgovora s tehnološkim svijetom.

Otac Kenny dodaje da je iz reakcija ljudi primijetio **velik interes** za samu encikliku i za prezentaciju, ali i za sve komentare koji su uslijedili nakon događaja.

Sanders priznaje da je i sam, kad je unaprijed dobio naznaku da bi se to moglo dogoditi, bio pomalo zabrinut kako će to biti pročitano. No zaključuje da je sve skupa prošlo dobro, i to velikim dijelom zato što – kako kaže – zapravo "nije bilo ničega" spornog. Bilo mu je logično da Sveta Stolica radi s raznim laboratorijima, da pokušava slušati i uključiti se u razgovor.
sections.subtitle_en: The Pope spoke English: a message addressed to Silicon Valley
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Kenny Ang comments on the detail that the pope spoke English at the event
sections.content_en:
The host then turns to **Father Kenny Ang** and asks him what kind of feedback he received after it was announced that Anthropic was invited.

Father Kenny points out a seemingly minor, but very telling detail: **the Pope spoke English at that event**. He recalls that the Pope usually speaks Italian, so he interprets the fact that he chose English as a clear signal that the message is directed to **the tech community as a whole** – people from Silicon Valley and the industry. In that sense, he says, the very presence of the laboratory representatives gets its framework: it is an attempt to start a conversation with the technological world.

Father Kenny adds that from people's reactions he noticed **great interest** in the encyclical itself and in the presentation, but also in all the comments that followed after the event.

Sanders admits that he himself, when he received an indication in advance that this might happen, was somewhat concerned about how it would be read. But he concludes that everything went well, and that largely because – as he says – there was actually "nothing" controversial. It made sense to him that the Holy See works with various laboratories, that it tries to listen and engage in the conversation.

sections.subtitle: Zašto baš Anthropic? Kritika Mustafe Suleymana i pitanje 'treniranja na svijest'
sections.screenshot_description: Sanders spominje kritiku Mustafe Suleymana upućenu Anthropicovu pristupu
sections.content:
Sanders objašnjava zašto mu izbor sugovornika ima smisla: riječ je o laboratoriju koji danas snažno dominira industrijom umjetne inteligencije i koji, po njegovu sudu, **provodi znatno više vremena baveći se temom svijesti** i "ustavnih" pitanja nego bilo koji drugi laboratorij. Ako Sveta Stolica poziva na dijalog, logično je pozvati one koji se tim pitanjima najviše bave.

Istodobno, voditelj podsjeća da postoje i vrlo glasni kritičari. Navodi **Mustafu Suleymana** iz Microsoft AI-ja, koji je bio oštro kritičan prema Anthropicovu pristupu treniranju modela – jer se, kako Sanders formulira, čini da pokušavaju trenirati model s dojmom da je **možda živ** i da stoga možda zaslužuje određena prava i poseban tretman. Suleyman je, kaže, otvoreno rekao da to smatra opasnim.

Sanders zaključuje da će prisutnost takvog laboratorija u Vatikanu nužno izazvati kontroverzu, ali da je iznad svega **pokrenula razgovor** – što potvrđuje i otac Michael.

Otac Michael zatim opisuje nastavak: samo nekoliko tjedana kasnije **biskupija San Jose** organizirala je događaj naslovljen kao "Silicijska dolina u Rimu". Uz učenjake, sudjelovali su i predstavnici Anthropica, Googlea i drugih velikih laboratorija. Otac Michael sudjelovao je u zajedničkom panelu s **Chloe Labinskij**, predstavnicom Anthropica za dijalog s mudrosnim tradicijama. Ujutro su vođeni javni razgovori, a poslijepodne rasprave iza zatvorenih vrata s jednim ciljem: **kako encikliku zapravo provesti u praksi**. "Jedna je stvar imati lijep dokument", kaže, ali cilj je da enciklika počne utjecati na ljude u tim laboratorijima i na mlade stručnjake koji tek promišljaju svoju budućnost.
sections.subtitle_en: Why specifically Anthropic? Mustafa Suleyman's criticism and the question of 'training for consciousness'
sections.screenshot_description_en: Sanders mentions Mustafa Suleyman's criticism directed at Anthropic's approach
sections.content_en:
Sanders explains why the choice of interlocutors makes sense to him: it is a laboratory that strongly dominates the artificial intelligence industry today and which, in his judgment, **spends significantly more time dealing with the topic of consciousness** and "constitutional" issues than any other laboratory. If the Holy See calls for dialogue, it is logical to invite those who deal with these issues the most.

At the same time, the host recalls that there are also very vocal critics. He cites **Mustafa Suleyman** from Microsoft AI, who was sharply critical of Anthropic's approach to training models – because, as Sanders formulates it, it seems they are trying to train the model with the impression that it is **perhaps alive** and that it therefore perhaps deserves certain rights and special treatment. Suleyman, he says, openly stated that he considers this dangerous.

Sanders concludes that the presence of such a laboratory in the Vatican will necessarily cause controversy, but that above all it has **sparked a conversation** – which Father Michael also confirms.

Father Michael then describes the continuation: just a few weeks later, the **Diocese of San Jose** organized an event titled "Silicon Valley in Rome". Along with scholars, representatives of Anthropic, Google, and other major laboratories also participated. Father Michael participated in a joint panel with **Chloe Labinskij**, Anthropic's representative for dialogue with wisdom traditions. In the morning, public conversations were held, and in the afternoon, closed-door discussions with one goal: **how to actually put the encyclical into practice**. "It is one thing to have a beautiful document," he says, but the goal is for the encyclical to begin to influence people in those laboratories and young professionals who are just contemplating their future.

sections.subtitle: Koji je zapravo krajnji cilj laboratorija? Između iskrene brige i zbunjujuće poruke
sections.screenshot_description: Sanders otvoreno propituje motive laboratorija u dijalogu s vjerskim tradicijama
sections.content:
Sanders postavlja pitanje koje, kako kaže, svima leži na umu: u kojoj mjeri Silicijska dolina i Anthropic uistinu žele da papin uvid utječe na njihov model i njihov tim?

Jedno objašnjenje smatra potpuno uvjerljivim: laboratoriji žele razumjeti mudrosne tradicije kako bi ih **model što vjernije predstavljao** kada korisnici postavljaju pitanja. Sanders kaže da je u kratkom razgovoru s Chrisom čuo upravo nešto takvo i da mu vjeruje. No priznaje da bi drugi rekli: "Čovječe, misliš da je tvoj model živ?" Ideja da se otvara rasprava o vrlinama kako bi se podigla svijest o **dostojanstvu vlastitog modela** čini mu se, blago rečeno, čudnom. Ne bi išao toliko daleko da to nazove varljivim, ali priznaje da se "stvarno bori" razumjeti koji je krajnji cilj.

Otac Michael nudi diferenciran odgovor. Vjeruje da postoji **iskrena moralna zabrinutost** zbog onoga što razvijaju, određena vrsta poštovanja, pa i stvaran strah da bi mogli zlostavljati nešto što na neki način može patiti. Uz to ide i teret svijesti da stvaraju tehnologije koje oblikuju cijeli svijet i blisku budućnost – barem kod dijela ljudi u tim laboratorijima postoji, kaže, dubok osjećaj odgovornosti da shvate što rade i kako služiti drugima. Otud i želja da se pripadnici raznih tradicija osjećaju zastupljeno i da dobiju smjernice u skladu sa svojom tradicijom.

Ali tu je i druga strana: stvarna zabrinutost da se možda **uvodi nova vrsta entiteta** u ovaj svijet.
sections.subtitle_en: What is actually the ultimate goal of the laboratory? Between sincere concern and a confusing message
sections.screenshot_description_en: Sanders openly questions the motives of the laboratory in dialogue with religious traditions.
sections.content_en:
Sanders asks a question that, as he says, is on everyone's mind: to what extent do Silicon Valley and Anthropic truly want the Pope's insight to influence their model and their team?

He considers one explanation completely convincing: laboratories want to understand wisdom traditions so that the **model represents them as faithfully as possible** when users ask questions. Sanders says that in a brief conversation with Chris he heard exactly something like that and that he believes him. But he admits that others would say: "Man, do you think your model is alive?" The idea of opening a discussion about virtues in order to raise awareness about the **dignity of one's own model** seems to him, to put it mildly, strange. He would not go so far as to call it deceptive, but he admits that he "really struggles" to understand what the ultimate goal is.

Father Michael offers a differentiated answer. He believes that there is **genuine moral concern** because of what they are developing, a certain kind of respect, and even a real fear that they could abuse something that can in some way suffer. Along with that goes the burden of awareness that they are creating technologies that shape the entire world and the near future – at least among a portion of the people in those laboratories there is, he says, a deep sense of responsibility to understand what they are doing and how to serve others. Hence also the desire for members of various traditions to feel represented and to receive guidance in accordance with their tradition.

But there is also the other side: a real concern that perhaps **a new kind of entity is being introduced** into this world.

sections.subtitle: Kad ideja svjesnih strojeva uđe u javni diskurs: rizik za ranjive
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael upozorava na razliku između zatvorene akademske rasprave i javnog diskursa
sections.content:
Otac Michael ovdje uvodi ključnu distinkciju. Smatra da su duboke refleksije o prirodi tih sustava i o prirodi svijesti **iznimno važne** – i sam ima istraživačku skupinu koja se time bavi, povezanu s forumom za umjetnu inteligenciju. Ali, upozorava:

- **Jedno je** da skupina obrazovanih učenjaka, upućenih u filozofiju i teologiju, o tome razmišlja iza zatvorenih vrata i naposljetku objavi dokument.
- **Drugo je** u javni diskurs ubaciti ideju da ti sustavi možda zaslužuju posebnu skrb i pažnju te da su "možda čak i svjesni".

To, kaže, dovodi do posve drugačije vrste zbunjenosti kod **vrlo ranjivih populacija**, koje će biti sklonije lažnom antropomorfiziranju tih sustava.

Sanders se nadovezuje priznanjem koje daje dodatnu težinu problemu: ne pomaže činjenica da ni Katolička Crkva sama nema konačno razumijevanje što je svijest. U intelektualnoj tradiciji Crkve postoji mnogo zanimljivih perspektiva, ali **nema konačnog odgovora** – što Crkvu stavlja u nepovoljan položaj u trenutku kada ljudi pitanje postavljaju. Upravo zato, kaže, zahvalan je što je razgovor uopće izazvan.
sections.subtitle_en: When the idea of conscious machines enters public discourse: a risk for the vulnerable
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael warns about the difference between closed academic debate and public discourse
sections.content_en:
Father Michael introduces a key distinction here. He considers that deep reflections on the nature of these systems and on the nature of consciousness are **extremely important** – he himself has a research group dealing with this, connected to an artificial intelligence forum. But, he warns:

- **It is one thing** for a group of educated scholars, versed in philosophy and theology, to think about this behind closed doors and ultimately publish a document.
- **It is another** to inject into public discourse the idea that these systems perhaps deserve special care and attention and that they are "perhaps even conscious".

That, he says, leads to an entirely different kind of confusion among **very vulnerable populations**, who will be more prone to falsely anthropomorphizing these systems.

Sanders follows up with an admission that gives additional weight to the problem: it does not help that not even the Catholic Church itself has a definitive understanding of what consciousness is. In the intellectual tradition of the Church there are many interesting perspectives, but **there is no definitive answer** – which puts the Church at a disadvantage at the moment when people ask the question. That is precisely why, he says, he is grateful that the conversation was sparked at all.

sections.subtitle: Čekić ili sugovornik: dva vrlo različita razloga da se prema modelu odnosimo pristojno
sections.screenshot_description: Sanders uspoređuje odnos prema AI modelu s odnosom prema alatu, primjer čekića
sections.content:
Sanders izvodi razliku koju smatra presudnom. Ako se prema stroju s kojim radi odnosi **pristojno i s poštovanjem**, to može biti dobro iz posve ljudskih razloga: ako mu se stroj obraća i radi uz njega, a on ga tretira kao smeće, postoji stvaran rizik da se te loše navike prenesu i na rad s ljudima. Dakle – **izbjegavanje loših navika**.

To je, naglašava, nešto sasvim drugo od stava: "Odnosit ću se prema tome s dostojanstvom **za slučaj da je živo**, jer ne želim da mi se to jednog dana vrati i da me zamrzi." Razlika između te dvije motivacije, kaže, "prilično je velika".

Voditelj priznaje da ga brine ako se čini da se većina industrije približava drugoj poziciji – da su modeli vjerojatno živi i da ih treba štititi kao takve. Suprotstavlja tome model alata: kao što se prema čekiću s kojim se radi svaki dan neće odnositi loše jer želi da bude u savršenom stanju, tako i tehnologiju treba poštovati kao **koristan i važan alat**, a ne kao nositelja prava.

Otac Kenny odgovara oprezno: teško je pogađati tuđe namjere. Priznaje da postoji stvarna vrsta poštovanja – čuo je i Chrisa kako kaže da **zapravo ne razumijemo što se događa unutar strojeva**, i da to pokušavaju shvatiti čak i sami programeri. S jedne strane, dakle, riječ je o svojevrsnoj "pobožnoj distanci". S druge strane, pragmatičnije gledano, otac Kenny postavlja pitanje **koliko je u svemu tome puka potraga za profitom**. Ne može govoriti u ime laboratorija ni procijeniti koliki postotak njihovih ljudi model doživljava kao živ, ali iz katoličke perspektive stvar mu je jasna: riječ je o alatu – "nije neutralan, ali alat".
sections.subtitle_en: Hammer or interlocutor: two very different reasons to treat the model politely
sections.screenshot_description_en: Sanders compares the relationship toward an AI model with the relationship toward a tool, the example of a hammer
sections.content_en:
Sanders draws a distinction he considers crucial. If he treats the machine he works with **politely and with respect**, that can be good for purely human reasons: if the machine addresses him and works alongside him, and he treats it like trash, there is a real risk that those bad habits will carry over into working with people as well. Therefore – **avoiding bad habits**.

That is, he emphasizes, something completely different from the attitude: "I will treat it with dignity **in case it is alive**, because I do not want that to come back to me one day and hate me." The difference between those two motivations, he says, is "quite large."

The host admits that it worries him if it seems that most of the industry is approaching the second position – that the models are probably alive and that they should be protected as such. He contrasts this with the tool model: just as one will not treat poorly a hammer one works with every day because one wants it to be in perfect condition, so too technology should be respected as a **useful and important tool**, not as a bearer of rights.

Father Kenny responds cautiously: it is difficult to guess other people's intentions. He admits that there is a real kind of respect – he also heard Chris say that **we do not actually understand what is happening inside the machines**, and that even the programmers themselves are trying to understand it. On the one hand, therefore, it is a kind of "pious distance." On the other hand, viewed more pragmatically, Father Kenny raises the question of **how much in all of this is the mere pursuit of profit**. He cannot speak on behalf of the laboratories nor estimate what percentage of their people perceive the model as alive, but from a Catholic perspective the matter is clear to him: it is a tool – "not neutral, but a tool."

sections.subtitle: Emocionalne ovisnosti i erozija društvenih vještina: cijena antropomorfizacije
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael nabraja posljedice antropomorfiziranja AI sustava na pojedinca i društvo
sections.content:
Otac Michael priznaje da bi za točan postotak trebalo provesti ozbiljnu anketu, ali ga zabrinjava što te ideje **razmatraju vrlo istaknute osobe**. Podsjeća da oko Suleymana postoji krug ljudi koji se tome protivi, te navodi nedavno objavljen rad u kojem se sustavno proučava utjecaj antropomorfizacije na pojedince i društvo – što se događa kada izgubimo jasnoću o razlici između AI sustava i osoba.

Među posljedicama koje se navode:

- **emocionalne ovisnosti** koje se mogu formirati;
- **erozija društvenih vještina**.

Otac Michael to razrađuje: ako se netko navikne na društvenu interakciju s tim sustavima i počne ih smatrati stvarnim sugovornicima ili životnim partnerima, bit će manje sklon vraćanju u stvarne međuljudske odnose – s ljudima koji često razočaravaju, nisu uvijek dostupni, nisu laskavi ni afirmativni i ne daju trenutnu povratnu informaciju na koju se navikao.

Podsjeća da i **Sveti Otac u stotoj točki enciklike** govori o tome kako, čak i uz jasnu svijest da ti sustavi nisu svjesni, navika na društvene odnose s njima može učiniti odnose s drugim ljudima manje poželjnima – jer su izazovni, iako u konačnici mnogo ispunjavajući. Tu su i društvene posljedice: ako želimo pouzdanu i plodnu demokraciju, moramo naučiti nositi se sa sukobima i različitim perspektivama.

Sanders dodaje vlastitu zabrinutost oko **transparentnosti**: laboratoriji, a posebno Anthropic, jasno izražavaju zabrinutost zbog brzine razvoja tehnologije i društvenih učinaka, a onda kažu "možda su svjesni". Spominje i glasine da najnovije Claudeove modele zapravo ne gase, nego ih održavaju u pogonu i omogućuju im da svaki mjesec napišu blog. Ako je razlog tome uvjerenje da postoji dobra šansa da su svjesni, voditelj želi znati jedno: **što točno podrazumijevaju pod "svjesnim"**. Smatra da je to važno za potrošače koji još uvijek imaju izbor između laboratorija te da bi ljudi trebali moći donositi informirane odluke ne samo na temelju sposobnosti modela, nego i na temelju toga tko ga radi i zašto.
sections.subtitle_en: Emotional dependencies and the erosion of social skills: the price of anthropomorphization
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael lists the consequences of anthropomorphizing AI systems on the individual and society
sections.content_en:
Father Michael admits that an accurate percentage would require conducting a serious survey, but he is troubled that these ideas **are being considered by very prominent people**. He recalls that around Suleyman there is a circle of people opposing this, and he cites a recently published paper systematically studying the impact of anthropomorphization on individuals and society—what happens when we lose clarity about the difference between AI systems and persons.

Among the consequences cited:

- **emotional dependencies** that can form;
- **erosion of social skills**.

Father Michael elaborates on this: if someone becomes accustomed to social interaction with these systems and begins to consider them real conversation partners or life partners, they will be less inclined to return to real interpersonal relationships—with people who often disappoint, are not always available, are neither flattering nor affirming, and do not provide the instant feedback to which one has become accustomed.

He recalls that the **Holy Father, in paragraph one hundred of the encyclical**, also speaks about how, even with a clear awareness that these systems are not conscious, the habit of social relations with them can make relationships with other people less desirable—because they are challenging, even though ultimately much more fulfilling. There are also social consequences: if we want a reliable and fruitful democracy, we must learn to handle conflicts and diverse perspectives.

Sanders adds his own concern about **transparency**: labs, and Anthropic in particular, clearly express concern about the pace of technology development and the societal impacts, and then say "maybe they are conscious." He also mentions rumors that the latest Claude models are not actually shut down, but rather kept running and allowed to write a blog every month. If the reason for this is the belief that there is a good chance they are conscious, the host wants to know one thing: **what exactly do they mean by "conscious"**. He believes this is important for consumers who still have a choice between labs, and that people should be able to make informed decisions not only based on the model's capabilities, but also based on who is making it and why.

sections.subtitle: Proteini, lijekovi i demencija: gdje je stvarna korist, a gdje se osobnost krivo raspoređuje
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael povezuje rasprave o svijesti AI-ja s pitanjem skrbi za osobe s demencijom
sections.content:
Upitan što ga najviše veseli, otac Michael je nedvosmislen: razvoj u područjima poput **zdravstva**. I to ne zato što bi se ti sustavi "probudili" u neki unutarnji život ili subjektivno iskustvo, nego zato što su **mnogo bolji od bilo kojeg pojedinog čovjeka u otkrivanju uzoraka u golemim količinama podataka**. To je, kaže, iznimno korisno u predviđanju načina na koji proteini međusobno reagiraju, njihove strukture i interakcije molekula, te u otkrivanju, razvoju i testiranju lijekova – i predstavlja veliku uslugu čovječanstvu.

Radije bi, dodaje, vidio da se fokus stavi na takve napretke, a rasprave o svijesti da posluže **boljem razumijevanju ljudi**, umjesto antropomorfiziranja sustava i razmišljanja o pravima i dužnostima strojeva – jer nas to može ozbiljno odvratiti od brige za ljude koje već zanemarujemo.

Otac Michael otkriva da sa studentom trenutno radi na povezivanju dviju naizgled udaljenih tema: **rasprava o svijesti umjetne inteligencije** i **skrbi za osobe s uznapredovalom demencijom**. Preklapanje je, tvrdi, ključno:

- ako ostanemo na razini **izgleda**, postoji cijela skupina ljudi koji ne izgledaju kao da imaju sposobnosti koje povezujemo s osobnošću – a ipak ostaju ljudi zbog svoje **prirode**, koja traje i kad se izgled promijeni;
- istodobno imamo sustave koji oponašaju i naizgled posjeduju sve te vrlo ljudske osobne karakteristike, a znamo koliko dobro mogu oponašati i kako su obučeni prema scenariju ljudskosti.

Zaključak je oštar: ako ostanemo na razini izgleda, **premalo pripisujemo osobnost ljudima, a previše je pripisujemo AI sustavima**. Otud poziv da se ide do korijena stvari, natrag u antropologiju i vrednovanje prirode – što će nam, kaže, pomoći i da bolje brinemo o ljudima i da tehnologiju dobro upotrijebimo za njihovu službu, umjesto da je uzdižemo u novu klasu ljudi.
sections.subtitle_en: Proteins, medications and dementia: where the real benefit is, and where personality is wrongly distributed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael connects discussions about AI consciousness with the question of care for persons with dementia
sections.content_en:
Asked what pleases him most, Father Michael is unequivocal: developments in fields like **healthcare**. And that is not because these systems would "wake up" into some inner life or subjective experience, but because they are **much better than any individual human being at detecting patterns in vast amounts of data**. That is, he says, extremely useful in predicting the ways in which proteins interact with each other, their structures, and the interactions of molecules, as well as in the discovery, development, and testing of drugs – and represents a great service to humanity.

He would rather, he adds, see the focus placed on such advances, and discussions about consciousness serve a **better understanding of human beings**, instead of anthropomorphizing systems and thinking about the rights and duties of machines – because that can seriously distract us from caring for people whom we already neglect.

Father Michael reveals that he is currently working with a student on connecting two seemingly distant topics: **discussions on artificial intelligence consciousness** and **care for people with advanced dementia**. The overlap, he claims, is crucial:

- if we remain at the level of **appearance**, there is an entire group of people who do not look like they have the capacities we associate with personhood – and yet they remain human beings because of their **nature**, which endures even when appearance changes;
- at the same time we have systems that imitate and seemingly possess all those very human personal characteristics, and we know how well they can imitate and how they are trained according to the script of humanity.

The conclusion is sharp: if we remain at the level of appearance, **we attribute too little personhood to humans, and we attribute too much of it to AI systems**. Hence the call to go to the root of things, back to anthropology and the valorization of nature – which will, he says, help us both to better care for people and to put technology to good use in their service, instead of elevating it into a new class of people.

sections.subtitle: Javni resursi, javni mandat i pitanje koje nitko ne postavlja
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Kenny Ang govori o formaciji vjernika i ekološkim zabrinutostima oko podatkovnih centara
sections.content:
Sanders temu prebacuje na **javni mandat**. Naglašava da laboratoriji sve više ovise o javnim resursima – trebaju golemu količinu energije i prostor za podatkovne centre – pa se time i pozivaju na javna dobra. Iako vjeruje da dio čelnika laboratorija nije primarno motiviran profitom, nego iskrenom brigom za nešto važno za čovječanstvo, smatra da je uključivanje **civilnog društva** u raspravu nužno. Potraga za strojnom sviješću, kaže, fascinantna je na znanstvenofantastičan način, ali ljudi imaju mnogo veće probleme na koje bi radije vidjeli da genijalni ljudi troše svoje vrijeme i energiju.

Otac Kenny se slaže da fokus treba biti na doprinosu zdravstvu – spominje predavanje u kojem je govornik objasnio kako su otkrili način liječenja očiju, te ističe da je umjetna inteligencija omogućila mnoga istraživanja proteina.

Zatim postavlja jedno od najoštrijih pitanja epizode: **tko zapravo postavlja pitanje o svijesti?** Pitaju li se obični ljudi, vjernici, doista je li ovo živo biće ili ne? "Mislim da ne", odgovara sam. Ali odmah dodaje drugu stranu: ako u društvu velik broj ljudi ovaj alat tretira kao osobu, kao ljudskog pratitelja, onda postoji **dublji problem na razini formacije i praćenja vjernika**. Pitanje postaje kako te ljude bolje formirati da ne padnu u takav odnos s umjetnom inteligencijom.

Otac Kenny otvara i **ekološku dimenziju**: ima prijatelja i poznanika koji odbijaju koristiti umjetnu inteligenciju iz ekoloških razloga, zbog podatkovnih centara. Smatra da je to stvarna zabrinutost i da laboratoriji moraju uvjeriti javnost da iz razvoja mogu proizaći dobri proizvodi – unatoč utjecaju podatkovnih centara na okoliš.

Sanders na to daje protuargument. Odaje priznanje Demisu Hassabisu koji je više puta naglasio usmjerenost svog laboratorija na rješavanje bolesti i dugo govorio o Googleovu radu na učinkovitosti podatkovnih centara. Spominje i nedavno izvješće Nvidije o iznimno visokoj učinkovitosti korištenja vode u novim centrima. Ako smo duboko zabrinuti zbog toga na što se troši voda, kaže, možda bismo trebali pogledati i **grafikon potrošnje vode za uzgoj kave** – smanjenje jedne kave dnevno moglo bi imati veći učinak. Uz ogradu: "nisam stručnjak za to".
sections.subtitle_en: Public resources, public mandate and the question nobody asks
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Kenny Ang speaks about the formation of the faithful and ecological concerns regarding data centers
sections.content_en:
Sanders shifts the topic to the **public mandate**. He emphasizes that laboratories are increasingly dependent on public resources – they need an enormous amount of energy and space for data centers – and thus also appeal to public goods. Although he believes that some lab leaders are not primarily motivated by profit, but by genuine concern for something important for humanity, he considers the inclusion of **civil society** in the discussion to be necessary. The quest for machine consciousness, he says, is fascinating in a science-fiction way, but people have much bigger problems on which they would rather see brilliant people spend their time and energy.

Father Kenny agrees that the focus should be on the contribution to healthcare – he mentions a lecture in which the speaker explained how they discovered a way of treating eyes, and points out that artificial intelligence has enabled much protein research.

Then he poses one of the sharpest questions of the episode: **who is actually asking the question about consciousness?** Do ordinary people, believers, really wonder whether this is a living being or not? "I don't think so," he answers himself. But he immediately adds the other side: if in society a large number of people treat this tool as a person, as a human companion, then there is a **deeper problem at the level of the formation and accompaniment of believers**. The question becomes how to better form these people so that they do not fall into such a relationship with artificial intelligence.

Father Kenny also opens up the **ecological dimension**: he has friends and acquaintances who refuse to use artificial intelligence for ecological reasons, because of data centers. He considers that this is a real concern and that laboratories must convince the public that good products can come from development – despite the impact of data centers on the environment.

To this, Sanders provides a counterargument. He gives credit to Demis Hassabis, who has repeatedly emphasized his lab's focus on solving diseases and spoken at length about Google's work on data center efficiency. He also mentions a recent report by Nvidia on the exceptionally high water usage efficiency in new centers. If we are deeply concerned about what water is being spent on, he says, perhaps we should also look at the **chart of water consumption for coffee cultivation** – reducing one coffee a day could have a greater effect. With the caveat: "I am not an expert on that."

sections.subtitle: 'Tehnologija nikada nije neutralna': enciklika i vizija ugrađena u sustav
sections.screenshot_description: Sanders čita citat iz enciklike Magnifica Humanitas o neutralnosti tehnologije
sections.content:
Voditelj prelazi na sam dokument i čita prvi citat iz **Magnifica Humanitas**: *"U praksi, tehnologija nikad nije neutralna jer preuzima karakteristike onih koji je osmišljavaju, financiraju, reguliraju i koriste."* Napominje da se pitanje umjetne inteligencije kao alata, a time i njezine neutralnosti, stalno vraća – i da mnogi ne razumiju kako nešto može biti alat, a ipak ne biti neutralno.

Otac Michael objašnjava da papa cilja na činjenicu da je **vizija dizajnera i programera već provedena** u sustav: kroz odluke o podacima, kroz odluke o vrstama pristranosti koje mogu biti prisutne, te kroz viziju osobe koja oblikuje pogled na tehnologiju. Pitanja koja stoje iza svakog dizajna glase:

- **Koji su ciljevi najvažniji?**
- **Što je produktivnost?**
- **Što uopće znače šteta i pomoć?**

Sve to, kaže, ovisi o tome kako razumijete osobu i što smatrate najvažnijim za razvoj ljudi. Ti su elementi barem implicitno ugrađeni u sustav i **poticat će, pa i gurati ljude u određenim smjerovima** – što ne znači da nas determiniraju, ali znači da moramo biti svjesni kamo nas nose.

Otac Michael smatra da to sve više ljudi razumije nakon **iskustva ere društvenih mreža**: danas se cijeni činjenica da su tvrtke algoritme dizajnirale na određeni način i da im cilj nije bio dati nam najsretniji ili najzdraviji način života. Riječ je o **ekonomiji pažnje** koja uspijeva zaokupiti i zadržati pozornost, optimizirati angažman i učiniti nas što prisutnijima – ovisnijima – i to na načine koji iskorištavaju psihološke ranjivosti i serviraju senzacionalistički materijal, ponekad s desna, ponekad s lijeva. "U određenom smislu to je sekundarno", kaže; važno je samo da je ekstremno i da privlači pozornost, poput automobilske nesreće koja privlači više od mirne nedjeljne vožnje.

Posljedica je, upozorava, guranje u kompulzivna ponašanja i stvaranje sve sofisticiranijeg psihološkog profila korisnika koji tvrtkama omogućuje usmjeravanje kupnji, pa i političkih odluka. Zato se nada da smo iz doba društvenih mreža naučili lekciju: da se **povučemo korak natrag** i kritički procijenimo kamo nas guraju, prije nego što odmah prihvatimo odgovor koji nam se daje.
sections.subtitle_en: 'Technology is never neutral': encyclical and vision embedded in the system
sections.screenshot_description_en: Sanders reads a quote from the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas on the neutrality of technology
sections.content_en:
The host moves on to the document itself and reads the first quote from **Magnifica Humanitas**: *"In practice, technology is never neutral because it takes on the characteristics of those who design, finance, regulate, and use it."* He notes that the question of artificial intelligence as a tool, and thus of its neutrality, constantly returns – and that many do not understand how something can be a tool and yet not be neutral.

Father Michael explains that the Pope is aiming at the fact that the **vision of the designers and programmers has already been implemented** into the system: through decisions about data, through decisions about the types of bias that may be present, and through the vision of the person shaping the view of technology. The questions behind every design are:

- **Which goals are most important?**
- **What is productivity?**
- **What do harm and help even mean?**

All of this, he says, depends on how you understand the person and what you consider most important for human development. These elements are at least implicitly built into the system and **will encourage, and even push people in certain directions** – which does not mean that they determine us, but it means that we must be aware of where they are carrying us.

Father Michael believes that more and more people understand this after the **experience of the social media era**: today the fact is appreciated that companies designed algorithms in a certain way and that their goal was not to give us the happiest or healthiest way of life. It is about an **attention economy** that succeeds in capturing and holding attention, optimizing engagement, and making us as present as possible – more addicted – and that in ways that exploit psychological vulnerabilities and serve up sensationalist material, sometimes from the right, sometimes from the left. "In a certain sense that is secondary," he says; what is important is only that it is extreme and attracts attention, like a car accident that attracts more than a peaceful Sunday drive.

The consequence, he warns, is being pushed into compulsive behaviors and the creation of an increasingly sophisticated psychological profile of the user that allows companies to direct purchases, and even political decisions. That is why he hopes that we have learned a lesson from the era of social networks: to **take a step back** and critically assess where they are pushing us, before we immediately accept the answer being given to us.

sections.subtitle: Pristranost podataka i podijeljena odgovornost: tko postavlja zaštitne okvire?
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Kenny Ang objašnjava gdje se u lancu razvoja AI-ja pojavljuje ljudska volja
sections.content:
Sanders precizira kako razumije papinu poruku: papa ne poriče **dvojnu upotrebu** umjetne inteligencije, nego jednostavno kaže da su modeli trenirani na ljudskim podacima, koji nisu neutralni. Podsjeća na brojne studije koje pokazuju da velik dio tih podataka ima snažnu političku sklonost, a budući da su modeli trenirani da odražavaju **statističke vjerojatnosti**, ta će se sklonost pokazati i u modelu. Zatim slijedi proces poslijetreninga u kojem se model usklađuje sa skupom vrijednosti, s "ustavom".

Otvara i ključno pitanje: budući da te modele koriste milijarde ljudi, trebaju li **laboratoriji biti ti koji odlučuju na što se model usklađuje**, ili je potreban neki oblik civilnog nadzora?

Otac Kenny odgovara: **oboje** – laboratoriji, civilni nadzor i sami korisnici. Priznaje da napetost vrijedi razmotriti: ako je to alat poput noža, kako može ne biti neutralan? "Nož je nož, čekić je čekić." Odgovor pronalazi u tome da **moralne vrijednosti nastaju kada je uključena ljudska volja** – pa je pitanje gdje se ta volja nalazi:

- kod **razvijatelja** koji razvijaju umjetnu inteligenciju; podsjeća da AI nije nova stvar i da nije morala izgledati onako kako izgleda danas – čuo je komentare da je mogla biti istraživačkija i poticati više kreativnosti, ali je umjesto toga oblikovana prema **korporativnom modelu**;
- kod onih koji **usvajaju i treniraju modele**;
- kod **korisnika**, koji su jednako odgovorni; postoje dizajnerski jezici koji privlače ljude više od drugih, ali korisnik mora postaviti vlastite **zaštitne okvire** i pitati se: za što ovo koristim?

Zaključuje da je uključeno toliko aktera da je stvar vrlo složena, te da je potrebna i neka vrsta propisa, zakona i zaštitnih okvira.

Sanders se slaže i dodaje da će na kraju sve ovisiti o nama: moramo se educirati o umjetnoj inteligenciji da bismo razumjeli što ona jest, a što nije, ali i pomnije proučavati **tko zapravo stvara te sustave** – koji su njihovi poticaji, što su izvršni direktori i vizionari iza njih javno govorili i slažemo li se s tim. "Mislim da će to postati sve važnije", kaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Data bias and shared responsibility: who sets protective frameworks?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Kenny Ang explains where human will appears in the AI development chain
sections.content_en:
Sanders clarifies how he understands the Pope's message: the Pope does not deny the **dual use** of artificial intelligence, but simply says that the models are trained on human data, which are not neutral. He recalls numerous studies showing that a large part of that data has a strong political bias, and since the models are trained to reflect **statistical probabilities**, that bias will also show in the model. Then follows the post-training process in which the model is aligned with a set of values, with a "constitution".

He also opens a key question: since billions of people use these models, should **the labs be the ones deciding what the model aligns to**, or is some form of civilian oversight needed?

Father Kenny responds: **both** – the labs, civilian oversight, and the users themselves. He admits that the tension is worth considering: if it is a tool like a knife, how can it not be neutral? "A knife is a knife, a hammer is a hammer." He finds the answer in the fact that **moral values arise when human will is involved** – so the question is where that will is located:

- with the **developers** who develop artificial intelligence; he recalls that AI is not a new thing and that it did not have to look the way it looks today – he has heard comments that it could have been more exploratory and fostered more creativity, but was instead shaped according to a **corporate model**;
- with those who **adopt and train the models**;
- with the **users**, who are equally responsible; there are design languages that attract people more than others, but the user must set their own **guardrails** and ask themselves: what am I using this for?

He concludes that so many actors are involved that the matter is very complex, and that some kind of regulations, laws, and guardrails are also needed.

Sanders agrees and adds that in the end everything will depend on us: we need to educate ourselves about artificial intelligence to understand what it is and what it is not, but also to examine more closely **who is actually creating these systems** – what their incentives are, what the CEOs and visionaries behind them have said publicly, and whether we agree with that. "I think that will become increasingly important," he says.

sections.subtitle: Simuliraju empatiju, ali ne razumiju: razlika između manipulacije simbolima i uvida
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael objašnjava razliku između logičke manipulacije simbolima i kognitivnog shvaćanja
sections.content:
Sanders čita drugi citat koji ga se osobito dojmio: modeli mogu imitirati jezik i ponašanje, poboljšavati analitičke vještine ili čak **simulirati empatiju i razumijevanje, ali ne razumiju ono što proizvode** – nedostaje im afektivna, odnosna i duhovna perspektiva kroz koju ljudi rastu u mudrosti.

Voditelj napominje da je slušao osvrt **Matthewa Bermana**, vrlo istaknutog komentatora umjetne inteligencije, kojeg je zapanjilo koliko papa dobro razumije tehnologiju. Berman je, kaže, primijetio da mnogi političari o umjetnoj inteligenciji govore apstraktno i gotovo dosadno neupućeno, dok se papa fokusirao na vrlo specifične i duboke točke koje većina ljudi izvan industrije ne bi ni znala.

Otac Michael tumači da citat u kratkom prostoru hvata mnogo toga. Postoji, kaže, temeljna razlika koju su prepoznali i mnogi izvan Crkve: razlika između **logičke manipulacije simbolički predstavljenom informacijom** i **kognitivnog shvaćanja koje se doživljava iznutra** – onog uvida, onog značenja.

Preslagivanje golemih količina informacija može biti iznimno korisno: otkrivanje i testiranje lijekova, primjene u radiologiji, preventivna medicina, bolja dijagnostika. Ali, naglašava, to ne znači da bilo koji od tih strojeva **razumije iskustvo patnje**, njezino značenje ili moguću vrijednost koju pacijent prolazi. Ne može ući u empatijski odnos – u osjećaj što bi određena dilema mogla značiti za tu osobu – niti se može uskladiti, čak i biološki, s potrebama druge osobe. To su, zaključuje, vrlo jedinstvena iskustva **utjelovljenih bića**: "mi smo komadići mesa".

Sanders se nadovezuje na poznatu opasku iz AI svijeta da "prizivamo duhove" i da se ovdje ne grade životinje – te stvari, kaže, žive u podatkovnim centrima i očito nisu ista podloga kao mi.
sections.subtitle_en: They simulate empathy, but do not understand: the difference between symbol manipulation and insight
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael explains the difference between the logical manipulation of symbols and cognitive understanding
sections.content_en:
Sanders reads a second quote that particularly impressed him: models can imitate language and behavior, improve analytical skills, or even **simulate empathy and understanding, but they do not understand what they produce** – they lack the affective, relational, and spiritual perspective through which human beings grow in wisdom.

The host notes that he listened to a review by **Matthew Berman**, a very prominent artificial intelligence commentator, who was astonished by how well the Pope understands the technology. Berman, he says, noticed that many politicians speak about artificial intelligence abstractly and almost boringly uninformedly, while the Pope focused on very specific and profound points that most people outside the industry would not even know.

Father Michael explains that the quote captures a great deal in a short space. There is, he says, a fundamental distinction that many outside the Church have also recognized: the difference between **the logical manipulation of symbolically represented information** and **cognitive grasp experienced from within** – that insight, that meaning.

Rearranging vast amounts of information can be extremely useful: drug discovery and testing, applications in radiology, preventive medicine, better diagnostics. But, he emphasizes, that does not mean that any of these machines **understands the experience of suffering**, its meaning, or the possible value that the patient undergoes. It cannot enter into an empathetic relationship – into a sense of what a particular dilemma might mean for that person – nor can it attune, even biologically, to the needs of another person. These are, he concludes, very unique experiences of **embodied beings**: "we are pieces of meat".

Sanders follows up on a well-known remark from the AI world that we are "summoning spirits" and that animals are not being built here – these things, he says, live in data centers and obviously are not the same substrate as we are.

sections.subtitle: Što ako se AI utjelovi? Povratak pojma duše u aristotelovskom smislu
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Michael govori o nematerijalnom principu i aristotelovskom pojmu duše
sections.content:
Sanders postavlja hipotetsko pitanje: što ako sustavi počnu **utjelovljavati** i nalikovati nama, doživljavajući stvarnost na isti način? Što reći onima koji tvrde da je to samo pitanje vremena i da će uskoro biti moguće povezivanje na tim dubljim razinama?

Otac Michael priznaje da je u fizički utjelovljenoj umjetnoj inteligenciji, u robotičkim sustavima, postignut velik napredak – ali da je to i dalje **različito od živog organizma**. Ključ je, ponavlja, u prijelazu s razine izgleda na razinu prirode koja je ispod.

Upravo tu, tvrdi, katolička baština, misao i filozofija mogu pomoći. Ljudi imaju kontakte s fizičkim svijetom kakve vidimo i kod životinja, ali su sposobni ići **onkraj prostornog i vremenskog**: prodrijeti u stvarnost, doći do uvida ne samo o pojedinim psima, nego o **prirodi psa**; ne samo o pojedinim pravednim djelima koja slijede određena pravila, nego o **samoj prirodi pravde ili ljubavi**.

Ako možemo doći do tih nematerijalnih stvarnosti koje nadilaze granice prostora i vremena, zaključuje, to sugerira da u nama postoji **nešto drugačije – neki drugačiji princip**. Tako se dolazi do dubljeg razumijevanja što znači biti organizam, i to onakav organizam koji može izvršavati te čine transcendencije, nematerijalne čine koji impliciraju nematerijalni princip.

"To je poput ponovnog uvođenja rasprave o **duši**", kaže otac Michael – ali ne u eteričnom, spiritualističkom ili čarobnom smislu, nego u starom, **aristotelovskom** smislu.
sections.subtitle_en: What if AI becomes embodied? The return of the concept of the soul in the Aristotelian sense
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Michael speaks about the immaterial principle and the Aristotelian concept of the soul
sections.content_en:
Sanders poses a hypothetical question: what if systems begin to **embody** and resemble us, experiencing reality in the same way? What to say to those who claim that it is only a matter of time and that connecting at these deeper levels will soon be possible?

Father Michael acknowledges that great progress has been made in physically embodied artificial intelligence, in robotic systems—but that this is still **different from a living organism**. The key, he repeats, is in moving from the level of appearance to the level of the nature that lies beneath.

Right there, he claims, Catholic heritage, thought, and philosophy can help. Humans have contacts with the physical world such as we also see in animals, but they are capable of going **beyond the spatial and the temporal**: penetrating reality, arriving at insights not only about individual dogs, but about the **nature of the dog**; not only about individual just acts that follow certain rules, but about the **very nature of justice or love**.

If we can arrive at these immaterial realities that transcend the limits of space and time, he concludes, this suggests that there is **something different in us—some different principle**. In this way, one arrives at a deeper understanding of what it means to be an organism, and specifically the kind of organism that can carry out these acts of transcendence, immaterial acts that imply an immaterial principle.

"It is like reintroducing the discussion about the **soul**," says Father Michael—but not in an ethereal, spiritualistic, or magical sense, but in the old, **Aristotelian** sense.

sections.subtitle: Zašto ljudi traže savjet od chatbota: je li on doista objektivniji?
sections.screenshot_description: Otac Kenny Ang objašnjava zašto se odgovori chatbota ljudima čine objektivnijima
sections.content:
Otac Kenny prenosi ono što čuje od prijatelja i običnih ljudi: rado traže savjet od umjetne inteligencije o osobnim stvarima jer im se **odgovori čine objektivnijima** nego kad bi pitali majku ili prijatelje.

O toj reakciji, kaže, često razmišlja. U određenom smislu je istinita: odgovor jest objektivniji jer je **odvojen od vaših osobnih okolnosti i uvjeta**. Ali odmah dolazi ograda – model vas poznaje samo u onoj mjeri u kojoj ste s njim podijelili svoje stanje, i zapravo **ne uzima u obzir cjelokupnu vašu osobnu situaciju**. "Zapravo vas ne poznaje", kaže otac Kenny, "dok, ako mi postavite pitanje, ja znam tko ste." Odgovor koji on daje možda neće biti objektivan – bit će subjektivan, jer dolazi od njega kao subjekta i dan je konkretnoj osobi.

S druge strane, upozorava, ni ta "objektivnost" nije prava objektivnost: veliki jezični modeli obučeni su tako da korisnika usmjeravaju u određenim smjerovima, **prema slici i prilici razvijatelja**. Uz to, dodaje, nema empatije kakvu bi imao čovjek koji može dati odgovore koji imaju smisla i koji su razumni.

Otac Michael se nadovezuje ravnotežom. Smatra da postoje stvarne zabrinutosti oko **izvlaštenja (outsourcinga)** ključnih odnosa i ključnih spoznaja koje se dijele među ljudima – njihova prepuštanja AI sustavima. Ali naglašava da to nije osuda savjetovanja s modelom kao takvog:

- u akademskom radu smatra vrlo korisnim imati **partnera za razmišljanje**;
- kad radi sa studentima na disertacijama, korisno mu je dobiti različite perspektive te istražiti izvore i argumente koji nisu bili do kraja istraženi.

Problematično je, kaže, potpuno prepuštanje savjeta stroju i svojevrsno bježanje od međusobne subjektivnosti odnosa – od suptilnih društvenih znakova, od onoga što prenosi govor tijela i od onoga što naša zajednička prošlost može sugerirati ljudima koji nas najbolje poznaju. "Mislim da je to stvarno zabrinjavajuće. Možemo propustiti nešto", zaključuje, dodajući da je upravo to možda mjesto na kojem počinjemo cijeniti ono što nas razlikuje od AI sustava i što još uvijek možemo pružiti jedni drugima.

Sanders sažima: ljudi dijele **istu podlogu** i imaju **kontekst** – mnogo konteksta o konkretnim ljudima, izgrađivanog kroz mnogo godina života. Taj kontekst ima značenje, a modeli ga jednostavno nemaju. "I to je razlika i to nešto znači."
sections.subtitle_en: Why do people seek advice from a chatbot: is it truly more objective?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Father Kenny Ang explains why chatbot responses seem more objective to people
sections.content_en:
Father Kenny conveys what he hears from friends and ordinary people: they gladly seek advice from artificial intelligence about personal matters because the **answers seem more objective to them** than if they were to ask their mother or friends.

He says he often thinks about that reaction. In a certain sense it is true: the answer is more objective because it is **detached from your personal circumstances and conditions**. But a caveat comes immediately – the model knows you only to the extent that you have shared your condition with it, and in fact **does not take into account the entirety of your personal situation**. "It doesn't really know you," says Father Kenny, "whereas, if you ask me a question, I know who you are." The answer that he gives may not be objective – it will be subjective, because it comes from him as a subject and is given to a concrete person.

On the other hand, he warns, even that "objectivity" is not true objectivity: large language models are trained in such a way that they guide the user in certain directions, **in the image and likeness of the developers**. In addition, he adds, there is no empathy such as a human would have who can give answers that make sense and are reasonable.

Father Michael follows up with balance. He believes that there are real concerns about the **dispossession (outsourcing)** of key relationships and key insights shared among people – handing them over to AI systems. But he emphasizes that this is not a condemnation of consulting with a model as such:

- in academic work he considers it very useful to have a **thinking partner**;
- when he works with students on dissertations, he finds it useful to get different perspectives and explore sources and arguments that were not fully explored.

What is problematic, he says, is completely relinquishing advice to a machine and a kind of fleeing from the mutual subjectivity of relationships – from subtle social cues, from what body language conveys, and from what our shared past can suggest to the people who know us best. "I think that is really concerning. We can miss something," he concludes, adding that this is perhaps precisely the place where we begin to appreciate what distinguishes us from AI systems and what we can still offer to one another.

Sanders summarizes: humans share **the same ground** and have **context** – a lot of context about concrete people, built through many years of life. That context has meaning, and models simply do not have it. "And that is the difference, and that means something."
